description: Corrected Wingspan fixture for the installable boardgame-rules plugin. Original interpretations of setup, turn structure, scoring, habitats, bird-power types, Automa overview, and selected edge cases, grounded against the official Stonemaier FAQ and publisher-commissioned Rulepop. Not a complete rulebook and not the FAQ/errata overlay in wingspan-rules/.
coverage_boundary: Covers setup, the four basic actions, scoring, habitats, bird-power types, Automa overview, and selected edge cases for the English base game (1st Edition / 2020 printing). Exact card text, later printings, and expansion minutiae are out of scope. The European Expansion entry is overview-only and tagged with its own edition.

entries.title: General Setup
entries.summary: Each player takes a player mat, action cubes of one color (8 for 2-player, 7 for 3-player, 6 for 4-player), and a scorepad. Place 3 face-up bird cards in the bird tray. Shuffle the bird deck and place it face-down. Place the birdfeeder with all 5 food dice inside. Each player draws 5 bird cards and chooses how many to keep, but for each bird card kept beyond 5 total items (birds + food + bonus cards), they must discard one. Each player also gains 5 food tokens of their choice from the birdfeeder (taking the matching die faces) and draws 2 bonus cards, keeping 1. The first player is chosen randomly after all players have selected their starting cards, food, and bonus card. In a competitive variant, first player may be determined before selection instead.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.3-4; FAQ: first-player selection
source_locator.question: When do we choose the first player? Before or after players choose cards and food?

entries.title: Bonus Cards
entries.summary: During setup, each player draws 2 bonus cards and keeps 1, returning the unkept card to the bonus card deck. You begin the game with exactly 1 bonus card. Additional bonus cards can be gained later through certain bird powers. All bonus cards are scored at the end of the game, whether or not their conditions were met (unmet bonus cards score 0).

analog_hooks.likeness: Bonus cards work like Ticket to Ride destination tickets: a private objective you keep secret and score at the end of the game.
analog_hooks.exception: An unmet Wingspan bonus card simply scores 0. It never subtracts points the way a failed destination ticket does.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.4; Rulepop: Bonus Cards

entries.title: Turn Structure Overview
entries.summary: The game lasts 4 rounds. Each round, players take turns in clockwise order. On your turn, choose exactly one of 4 actions: Play a Bird, Gain Food, Lay Eggs, or Draw Bird Cards. Place an action cube on the leftmost exposed slot of the corresponding row on your player mat. A round ends when all players have used all their action cubes for that round. The number of actions per round decreases each round, matching the columns on the player mat: in a 2-player game it is 8/7/6/5, in a 3-player game 7/6/5/4, and in a 4-player game 6/5/4/3 (round 1 through round 4). Between rounds, the first-player marker passes clockwise.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.5

entries.title: Gain Food Action
entries.summary: Place an action cube in the leftmost exposed slot of the Forest row on your player mat. Gain the amount of food shown on that slot (this increases as you fill the row from left to right). Take food from the birdfeeder by choosing dice one at a time; each die face shows a food type, and you take a matching food token. You may choose dice one at a time, with the option to reroll if conditions are met between selections. If all dice in the birdfeeder tray show the same face (including if only 1 die remains), you may first throw all 5 dice back in and reroll before gaining food; this is optional and free. If the tray is empty, throw all 5 dice back in automatically. After gaining food, activate any brown (When Activated) powers on your Forest birds, from right to left. All powers are optional. You can always decline a benefit, but you can never decline a cost.

analog_hooks.likeness: Food tokens are Wingspan's resources, like Catan's wood, brick, grain, ore, and wool: you stockpile them so you can pay costs later.
analog_hooks.exception: In Catan resources arrive passively when the dice roll matches your settlements, even on other players' turns. In Wingspan gaining food is an action you spend your whole turn on, picking dice out of the birdfeeder.

analog_hooks.likeness: The birdfeeder is a shared pool like Azul's factory displays: you draft dice out of it, what you take is gone until it refills, and watching what you leave for others matters.
analog_hooks.exception: You pick dice one at a time — there is no take-all-of-one-color rule — and the feeder refills only when it empties, or when every remaining die shows the same face and you choose the free reroll.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.5-6; FAQ: dice selection one at a time; Rulepop: The Birdfeeder
source_locator.question: When I gain food from the birdfeeder, do I choose all of the dice at once, or one by one?

entries.title: Lay Eggs Action
entries.summary: Place an action cube in the leftmost exposed slot of the Grassland row on your player mat. Lay the number of eggs shown on that slot (this increases as you fill the row from left to right). Place each egg on any bird on your player mat that has remaining egg capacity, distributed however you choose among eligible birds. A bird's egg capacity is printed on its card. If a bird is at capacity, no more eggs may be placed on it. There is no limit to the egg supply. After laying eggs, activate any brown (When Activated) powers on your Grassland birds, from right to left. All powers are optional.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.6; Rulepop: Eggs

entries.title: Draw Bird Cards Action
entries.summary: Place an action cube in the leftmost exposed slot of the Wetland row on your player mat. Draw the number of bird cards shown on that slot (this increases as you fill the row from left to right). For each card, you may draw from either the 3 face-up cards on the bird tray or from the top of the bird deck; you can look at each card before deciding where to draw the next one. When you take a face-up tray card, it is not refilled until the end of your turn. At the end of your turn, refill empty tray spaces from the deck. There is no hand limit. If the bird deck runs out during the game, reshuffle all discarded bird cards to form a new deck. At the end of each round, discard any remaining face-up tray cards and replenish with 3 new ones. After drawing, activate any brown (When Activated) powers on your Wetland birds, from right to left. All powers are optional.

analog_hooks.likeness: Drawing bird cards works like drawing train cards in Ticket to Ride: for each draw you choose between a face-up display (the 3-card bird tray) and the top of the deck, sight unseen.
analog_hooks.exception: Ticket to Ride refills the display immediately after each pick; the Wingspan bird tray refills at the end of your turn. There is no equivalent of the face-up locomotive costing both draws, and Wingspan has no hand limit.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.6; FAQ: drawing multiple cards; Rulepop: Draw Bird Cards
source_locator.question: What about when drawing multiple cards? Can I draw a card from the deck, look at it, and then decide where to continue drawing birds?

entries.title: Play a Bird Action
entries.summary: Place an action cube in the leftmost exposed slot of the Play a Bird row on your player mat. Pay the bird's food cost by spending matching food tokens from your personal supply (returned to the general supply, not the birdfeeder). Wild (star) food icons on the card can be paid with any food type. Then place the bird card in the leftmost exposed slot of one of your three habitats (Forest, Grassland, or Wetland). For columns 2 through 5, you must also spend the number of eggs printed on that column's slot, removing them from any of your played birds. There is no nest-type restriction on placement; nest type matters only for end-of-round goals and certain bird powers. Once a bird is played, it is permanent and cannot be discarded. Playing a bird does not activate any brown powers in that habitat.

analog_hooks.likeness: Playing a bird is Wingspan's pay-to-build, like spending wood and brick on a Catan settlement: pay the printed resource cost, place a permanent piece you cannot take back.
analog_hooks.exception: Birds go on your own player mat, not a shared map — there are no adjacency or placement-blocking rules. Birds in columns 2-5 also cost eggs on top of food, which has no Catan equivalent.

analog_hooks.likeness: Like claiming a route in Ticket to Ride, you pay a printed cost in collected resources (food tokens instead of matching train cards) to make a permanent placement, and wild (star) icons accept any food the way locomotives stand in for any color.
analog_hooks.exception: Birds are placed on your own mat, so nobody can claim a bird slot ahead of you the way a route gets taken. Columns 2-5 add an egg cost with no Ticket to Ride equivalent.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.7; FAQ: can you discard birds from your mat
source_locator.question: Can you discard birds from your player mat?

entries.title: End of Game Scoring
entries.summary: After round 4, score points in the following categories: (1) Birds: sum the victory points printed in the upper-left corner of each bird card on your mat. (2) Bonus cards: score each of your bonus cards per its condition. (3) End-of-round goals: points earned from goal tiles during the game. (4) Eggs: 1 point per egg on your birds. (5) Cached food: each food token cached on a bird (placed by a bird power) is worth 1 VP. (6) Tucked cards: each bird card tucked under a bird (by a flocking power) is worth 1 VP. Food tokens remaining in your personal supply and bird cards in your hand are worth 0 points. The player with the most total points wins. Ties are broken by most leftover food, then most leftover bird cards in hand.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.10; Rulepop: Cache and Bird Powers (tucked cards worth 1 VP)

entries.title: End-of-Round Goals
entries.summary: Each round has a goal tile revealed at the start of that round. Goals vary; examples include most eggs in a specific habitat, most birds in a habitat, or total wingspan in a habitat. After all players finish their turns and round-end (teal) powers resolve, score the goal. The first-place player earns the top-point token, second place earns the middle token, and so on. When players tie, they share the combined points of the tied positions, divided by the number of tied players, rounded down. The next player after a tie receives the next position's token. Goal tiles have two sides: one for 2-3 players (fewer positions scored) and one for 4+ players. Points are cumulative across rounds.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.3, 10

entries.title: Forest Habitat
entries.summary: The Forest habitat is associated with the Gain Food action. When you take Gain Food, place an action cube in the leftmost exposed slot of the Forest row and gain the amount of food shown on that slot. The food quantity increases as you fill the row from left to right. After gaining food, activate any brown (When Activated) powers on your Forest birds, resolving from right to left. The first column of the Forest row has no power-activation icon on the player mat, so birds in that column do not have their brown powers triggered. All brown powers are optional. You can always decline a benefit but never a cost.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.8; Rulepop: Bird Powers (When Activated, right to left)

entries.title: Grassland Habitat
entries.summary: The Grassland habitat is associated with the Lay Eggs action. When you take Lay Eggs, place an action cube in the leftmost exposed slot of the Grassland row and lay the number of eggs shown on that slot. The egg quantity increases as you fill the row from left to right. Place eggs on any of your birds with remaining capacity. After laying eggs, activate any brown (When Activated) powers on your Grassland birds, resolving from right to left. The first column of the Grassland row has no power-activation icon on the player mat, so birds in that column do not have their brown powers triggered. All brown powers are optional.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.8; Rulepop: Bird Powers (right to left)

entries.title: Wetland Habitat
entries.summary: The Wetland habitat is associated with the Draw Bird Cards action. When you take Draw Bird Cards, place an action cube in the leftmost exposed slot of the Wetland row and draw the number of cards shown on that slot. The card quantity increases as you fill the row from left to right. For each card, choose either a face-up tray card or the top of the deck. After drawing, activate any brown (When Activated) powers on your Wetland birds, resolving from right to left. The first column of the Wetland row has no power-activation icon on the player mat, so birds in that column do not have their brown powers triggered. All brown powers are optional.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.9; Rulepop: Bird Powers and Draw Bird Cards

entries.title: Bird Power Types
entries.summary: Bird powers come in five types, distinguished by the background color of the power icon: (1) When Played (no colored background, sometimes called white powers): activates only once, when the bird is played. (2) When Activated (brown): activates from right to left whenever you use the corresponding habitat action. (3) Once Between Turns (pink): triggers on opponents' turns, at most once between each of your own turns; it can even activate once after your final turn. (4) Round End (teal): resolved when all turns in the round are complete, before scoring the goal, in player order starting with the first player. (5) Game End (yellow): activates once at the end of the game, after all end-of-round steps. All bird powers are always optional. You can always decline a benefit but never a cost; to avoid a cost entirely, skip the power. Not all birds have powers. Birds in the first column of any habitat row do not have their brown powers activated (no power icon on the mat for that column).

analog_hooks.likeness: Pink (Once Between Turns) powers mean you are not fully idle while others play — the closest Catan feeling is staying engaged on other players' turns, the way their rolls can pay you resources or the active player can trade with you.
analog_hooks.exception: A pink power fires only when its specific trigger happens, and at most once between your own turns. It is not open-ended like Catan trading, and nothing in Wingspan is negotiated.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.7-8; FAQ: pink powers after final turn; Rulepop: Bird Powers
source_locator.question: Can I activate pink (Once Between Turns) powers after my final turn?

entries.title: Egg Capacity and Nests
entries.summary: Each bird card prints an egg capacity (the number of small egg icons on the card). A bird cannot hold more eggs than its capacity. When a bird reaches capacity, no more eggs may be placed on it. Eggs may be removed by spending them to play birds in columns 2-5 or by certain bird powers. Each egg on your birds at end of game is worth 1 VP. Nest types (cavity, platform, cup, ground, and star/wild) matter for end-of-round goals that score specific nest types and for certain bird powers that interact with nests. The star nest is wild and counts as any nest type for goals and powers. There is no limit to the egg supply.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.6, 10; Rulepop: Eggs

entries.title: Food Costs
entries.summary: Bird food costs are shown by icons on the left side of the card. Each food type required must be spent from your personal supply and returned to the general supply (not the birdfeeder). Wild (star) icons can be paid with any food type. The five food types are invertebrate, seed, fruit, fish, and rodent. For example, a bird costing two invertebrates requires spending 2 invertebrate tokens. A bird with a wild icon plus 1 fish requires 1 fish and 1 token of any type. You may use the 2-for-1 food rule (if playing with Oceania) or any other conversion only if a bird power or expansion rule explicitly permits it; in the base game, food costs must be paid exactly.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.7

entries.title: Birdfeeder and Dice
entries.summary: The birdfeeder is a shared dice tower containing 5 food dice. Each die has 6 faces showing food types: invertebrate, seed, fruit, fish, rodent, and a wild face (invertebrate-or-seed). The wild face is NOT fish; it is a distinct face showing both an invertebrate and a seed icon. When you gain food from the birdfeeder, choose dice one at a time and take the matching food token for each. If all dice remaining in the tray show the same face (including if only 1 die remains), and you are about to gain food for any reason, you may first throw all 5 dice back into the birdfeeder and reroll. This reroll is optional and free, regardless of whether the food is gained from a basic action or a bird power. If the birdfeeder tray is empty (all dice have been taken), throw all 5 dice back in automatically.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.5-6; FAQ: reroll from bird powers; Rulepop: The Birdfeeder (5 dice, same-face reroll)
source_locator.question: Can I reroll the dice in the birdfeeder if gaining food from a bird's power?

entries.title: Wingspan and Placement
entries.summary: Each bird card prints its wingspan in centimeters. Wingspan does NOT restrict where a bird can be placed; any bird can go in any habitat as long as you pay the food and egg costs. Wingspan matters for end-of-round goals that measure total wingspan in a habitat and for certain bird powers (such as hunting predators that compare wingspans). Some bird powers reference birds with wingspans above or below a specific threshold (e.g., under 30 cm or over 50 cm).

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.7

entries.title: End of Round
entries.summary: A round ends when all players have used all their action cubes for that round; there is no explicit pass action. After all players are done, resolve round-end (teal) powers in player order starting with the first player. Then score the end-of-round goal. Remove all action cubes from the goal board. Pass the first-player marker clockwise. Reveal the next round's goal tile. Discard any remaining face-up bird tray cards and replenish with 3 new ones. Begin the next round. Action cubes on the player mat remain in place for the entire game; they mark which slots have been used.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.9; Rulepop: Round End powers and bird tray replenishment

entries.title: Automa (Solo Mode)
entries.summary: In solo mode, you play against the Automa, a deck of cards that simulates an opponent. Set up your side of the game normally. The Automa does not use a player mat, bird cards, or food tokens; instead, it scores points each round based on Automa cards. For each of the 4 rounds, you always go first and the Automa always takes the last turn. After your turn, draw and resolve the top card of the Automa deck. At end of game, compare your score to the Automa's total; beat the Automa to win.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.11; FAQ: Automa who goes first
source_locator.question: Automa: Who goes first each round, you or the Automa?

entries.title: Tied End-of-Round Goals
entries.summary: When two or more players tie for a position in an end-of-round goal, they share the combined points of all tied positions, divided by the number of tied players, rounded down. The next player after the tie receives the next available position's points. Example with a 4/2/1 goal tile: 2 players tied for 1st get (4+2)/2 = 3 points each; the next player gets 1. If 3 players tie for 1st, they get (4+2+1)/3 = 2 points each (rounded down from 2.33); no one else scores.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.10

entries.title: Empty Birdfeeder and Reroll
entries.summary: Two distinct birdfeeder situations: (1) Empty tray: if all 5 dice have been taken from the birdfeeder tray, throw all 5 dice back in. This is automatic, not optional. (2) All same face: if all dice remaining in the tray show the same face (including if only 1 die remains), and you are about to gain food for any reason (basic action or bird power), you may first throw all 5 dice back in and reroll. This is optional and free. The wild face (invertebrate-or-seed) counts as its own unique face for this check. These rules apply whenever you have the opportunity to gain food from the birdfeeder, including from bird powers.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.5; FAQ: reroll from bird powers; Rulepop: The Birdfeeder
source_locator.question: Can I reroll the dice in the birdfeeder if gaining food from a bird's power? What about when there are qualifying terms such as 'if available' or 'if there is one?'

entries.title: Deck Exhaustion
entries.summary: If the bird card deck runs out during the game, reshuffle all discarded bird cards to form a new deck. The face-up bird tray is not disrupted; empty tray spaces are refilled at the end of the current player's turn as normal. Discarded cards include cards discarded during setup, cards discarded by bird powers, and any cards returned to the discard pile. At the end of each round, remaining face-up tray cards are discarded and replaced with 3 new cards from the (reshuffled) deck.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.6; Rulepop: Managing the bird deck

entries.title: Brown Power Timing
entries.summary: Brown (When Activated) powers activate from right to left, one bird at a time, whenever you take the corresponding habitat action. Each bird's power resolves fully before the next one activates. All brown powers are optional; you may skip any power to avoid its cost or because you do not want its benefit. Birds in the first column of a habitat row do not activate (no power icon on the mat). If a brown power gains a resource (food, egg, or card), that resource is available immediately for subsequent powers in the same activation sequence. Brown powers do not grant extra action cubes; the number of actions per round is fixed by the round and player count.

analog_hooks.likeness: Chaining brown powers right to left is engine-building like Dominion: each bird you add makes the same action produce more, and a resource one power generates is immediately available to the next power in the chain.
analog_hooks.exception: Your birds are a permanent tableau that fires in fixed row order every time you take the action — nothing cycles through a deck, so the engine is predictable rather than shuffle-dependent.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.8; FAQ: declining benefits; Rulepop: When Activated (right to left)
source_locator.question: Can I choose to lay fewer eggs, gain fewer food, or draw fewer eggs?

entries.title: Duplicate Bird Species
entries.summary: There is no rule preventing multiple copies of the same bird species from being played. Each bird card is a distinct individual, even if it shares a species name with another card. Multiple players can play the same species, and you can play the same species more than once on your own mat (space permitting).

source_locator.locator: rulebook (no restriction stated); FAQ: birds are permanent once played
source_locator.question: Can you discard birds from your player mat?

entries.title: Hand Limit
entries.summary: There is no hand limit for bird cards. You may hold as many bird cards as you wish. There is also no limit on food tokens in your personal supply. You are never forced to discard cards or food. The only way to reduce your hand or supply is through game actions and bird powers.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.6; Rulepop: Draw Bird Cards (no hand limit)

entries.title: Food Die Wild Face
entries.summary: The birdfeeder dice have 6 faces each: invertebrate, seed, fruit, fish, rodent, and a wild face. The wild face shows both an invertebrate and a seed icon. Fish is NOT the wild face; fish is a normal food type. When you choose a die showing the wild face, you gain either 1 invertebrate or 1 seed (your choice). The wild face counts as its own unique face for the all-same-face reroll check.

source_locator.locator: rulebook p.5; Rulepop: The Birdfeeder (invertebrate-or-seed counts as its own unique face)

entries.title: European Expansion Overview
entries.summary: The Wingspan: European Expansion adds new bird cards, a new player color (purple), additional bonus cards, and additional end-of-round goal tiles. Some European Expansion birds have new pink (Once Between Turns) powers that interact with other players, such as laying eggs on other players' birds or giving food to other players. Some birds count double toward end-of-round goals. The expansion is fully compatible with the base game and can be shuffled directly into the deck. It does NOT introduce a new resource type; the base game's five food types remain unchanged.

source_locator.locator: European Expansion rulebook p.2

entries.title: Migrating birds leave the action token behind
entries.summary: When a bird migrates, its action token stays in the row where the action began; apply the FAQ positional condition even if the original row has only that bird.
